prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Liberal Democrats present themselves as the open, tolerant and united alternative to an overmighty Conservative government and a failed Labour opposition. A vote for the Lib Dems is a vote to change the opposition and hold power to account on the NHS, education, the environment and Europe.

Protect Britain’s place in Europe: give the people a final say on the Brexit deal, with the option to remain. Fight a hard Brexit; keep the UK in the single market and customs union; unilaterally guarantee EU citizens’ rights (and secure the same for UK citizens in the EU); preserve freedom of movement, Erasmus+, policing and security cooperation, environmental and social protections, and support for science, business, travel and young people.

Save our NHS and social care: a 1p rise on Income Tax ringfenced for the NHS and care; genuine parity for mental health with waiting-time standards; integrate health and social care (“home not hospital”); back carers; end the NHS pay cap, protect EU staff and restore nurse bursaries.

Put children first: reverse school and college cuts, protect per‑pupil funding, strengthen the Pupil Premium and triple the Early Years Pupil Premium; oppose new grammars; empower and develop teachers; protect arts and a rich curriculum including life skills; improve SEND support; widen university access and reinstate maintenance grants; champion lifelong learning and high‑quality apprenticeships.

Build an economy that works for you: eliminate the day‑to‑day deficit by 2020 but borrow to invest £100bn in homes, hospitals and schools, hyperfast broadband, transport (HS2/HS3/Crossrail 2) and clean energy. Protect NHS and schools budgets; make taxes fairer, close avoidance and reform business rates; support SMEs and entrepreneurs; back innovation, green industries and the creative economy; modernise workers’ rights for the gig economy, promote a living wage, transparency on pay and employee ownership; spread opportunity to every region with real devolution and local banking.

Keep our country green: five green laws (transport, zero‑carbon, nature, buildings, zero‑waste); insulate 4m homes; a clean air plan with a diesel scrappage scheme and an end to sales of new diesel cars/vans by 2025; 60% of electricity from renewables by 2030; no fracking; net‑zero by 2050; protect nature and animal welfare; fair, sustainable farming and food standards; drive a circular, zero‑waste economy.

Support families and communities: expand free childcare from 9 months (prioritised) and flexible work from day one; fair welfare (scrap the two‑child limit and bedroom tax, uprate benefits, reverse ESA cuts); keep the pension triple lock; build 300,000 homes a year including new garden cities and 500,000 affordable, energy‑efficient homes; strengthen renters’ rights and end rough sleeping; invest in modern, accessible transport and rural broadband; back local culture and sport; devolve power to communities.

Defend rights, justice and liberty: stand by the Human Rights Act and ECHR; a Digital Bill of Rights; tackle hate crime; advance equality for women, BAME and LGBT+ people; humane drugs policy (end imprisonment for possession; regulate cannabis); smarter policing with community focus and victims’ rights; rehabilitation over short prison terms.

Immigration and asylum: make the positive case, run a fair, efficient system; restore post‑study work; create a Migration Impact Fund; offer safe routes for refugees, expand Syrian resettlement and the Dubs scheme; end indefinite detention.

Make a better world: proudly internationalist; defend multilateralism; spend 0.7% on aid; stricter arms controls (suspend sales to Saudi Arabia); commit 2% on defence, maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing disarmament; lead on human rights.

Fix a broken system: votes at 16, proportional representation for Westminster and local government, reform the Lords, curb big money, and deliver a federal UK through a constitutional convention and deeper devolution across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
